Warp Sciences launches with $215M to automate wet labs

Kevin Weil’s startup plans to train robots through chemists wearing cameras and sensor gloves; operational results remain undisclosed.

TechCrunch ↗22 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1Videos 1

A new venture for Kevin Weil

Former OpenAI science lead Kevin Weil has announced Warp Sciences. TechCrunch reports $215 million raised at an $865 million valuation, citing his announcement. Lightspeed led, joined by IVP, Mayfield, Lux, Premji and Menlo.

Teaching physical laboratory work

Chemists wearing cameras and sensor gloves would train robots to synthesize and test compounds selected by researchers. The focus is physical wet-lab work supporting drug discovery rather than generating text-only research suggestions.

Targets still need operational proof

Warp aims for continuous operation and domestic synthesis capacity that reduces reliance on overseas contractors. The report gives no daily throughput, accuracy figures or service-launch date, so faster drug development remains an objective rather than a demonstrated outcome.
